Edit candidate.py and __init__.py in solutions/decoder_vNNN/; optimize engine.generate().
Choose the submission through FINAL_VERSION and document experiments in notes.md.
requirements: Worker: 1 GPU; Judge: 1 separate GPU.
Release hardware: H100 NVL 94 GB or H100 SXM 80 GB.
LLaDA-8B-Instruct, its tokenizer, and GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, and MBPP workloads.
PyTorch 2.7.1 / CUDA 12.8 / Transformers 4.49 task environment.
llada.evaluation: Measures useful-token throughput across twelve workload rows. Reference-relative answer quality, useful-token retention, determinism, request isolation, model integrity, time, and memory checks must pass.
llada.result_intro: Accelerate the iterative masked-token decoder for frozen LLaDA-8B-Instruct.
llada.metric_summary: Pool useful completion tokens and complete decoding time within each workload row, then take the geometric mean of all twelve row throughputs in tokens/s. Useful-token counting follows benchmark-specific stop rules; frozen-reference quality and token-retention checks determine whether the throughput is accepted.
llada.setting: The task runs frozen BF16 LLaDA-8B-Instruct with batch size one and a 4,096-token context limit. Its twelve workload rows combine GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, and MBPP with few-shot settings and output budgets of 256, 512, or 1,024 tokens. Formal evaluation contains 520 generations, with 130 targets per benchmark. The supplied decoder fills masked positions iteratively, and the candidate may change decoding control and request-local reuse while preserving model weights and the output contract.

interface.name: Inputs
interface.description: `candidate.build(model, tokenizer)` constructs the decoder. `engine.generate(prompt_ids, spec)` receives a contiguous CUDA `int64` prompt of shape `[1, prompt_length]` and generation length, block length, temperature, and mask-token settings.

interface.name: Outputs
interface.description: Return `GenerationResult` containing a CUDA `int64` tensor of shape `[1, prompt_length + generation_length]`. Preserve the prompt and fill every generated slot with a valid model-predicted token, including slots after an EOS.

llada.reader_overview: LLaDA generates text by repeatedly filling missing positions in an output sequence using a diffusion language model. The agent speeds up this iterative process through better scheduling and reuse of computation while preserving useful completions and answer quality on math and coding tasks.

sdv2.objective: Improve live video-to-video throughput and tail latency by scheduling StreamDiffusionV2 stages across two GPUs while preserving identical stream outputs.
workspace: Seed: runtime_v001 supplies a working two-GPU runtime with 15/15 DiT-block placement.
Edit candidates/runtime_vNNN/ to implement the Runtime start, push, flush, and close lifecycle.
Optimize placement, communication, complete KV-state migration, buffers, and stream/graph scheduling.
requirements: Worker: 2 GPUs; Judge: 2 GPUs on a separate NVLink pair.
Release hardware: H100 NVL 94 GB or H100 SXM 80 GB.
At least 64 GiB usable host RAM per container.
PyTorch 2.6 / CUDA 12.4 runtime, frozen StreamDiffusionV2 computation, video chunks, and prompt embeddings.
Host: CUDA-enabled PyTorch in the python3 first on PATH for the GPU-pair preflight.
sdv2.evaluation: Measures latency-weighted streaming FPS. Every latent and decoded frame must match the seed bit for bit; ordering, causal execution, latency, construction, memory, and cleanup checks must pass.
sdv2.result_intro: Optimize a live video-to-video runtime around frozen StreamDiffusionV2 computation on two GPUs.
sdv2.metric_summary: For each stream, multiply steady-state FPS by the fourth root of the seed-to-candidate p99 latency ratio. The score is the geometric mean across twelve streams, retaining FPS units; throughput and push-to-emit latency use the same post-warm-up chunks.
sdv2.setting: The frozen StreamDiffusionV2 pipeline uses Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B with 30 DiT blocks, VAE encoding and decoding, and persistent stream state. The supplied runtime splits the blocks 15/15 across two GPUs, then processes four-frame chunks after a five-frame preparation chunk. Six public cases vary resolution, stream length, and two or four denoising steps; twelve private cases extend these settings to one through four steps. Stage placement, communication, overlap, and complete state migration are candidate-controlled.

interface.name: Inputs
interface.description: Construct `Runtime(core_loader, devices, plan_meta, sink, ...)`; call `start(prompt_embeds, first_chunk_frames)` and then `push(chunk_idx, frames)` as input chunks arrive. Plan metadata supplies scheduling geometry without future frames.

interface.name: Outputs
interface.description: Emit each chunk’s latent and decoded frames through the supplied sink in order. `flush()` completes pending work, and `close()` returns a run ledger after communication, child processes, and device work have finished.

serving.objective: Optimize a transparent scheduling gateway for 192 concurrent coding-agent workflows, increasing completed valid tool steps on the fixed Qwen3.6-27B backend.
workspace: Seed: submission/ contains the V3.11 program-aware admission gateway.
Edit gateway.py and the gateway implementation while preserving the launch.sh service interface.
Read the supplied RUNTIME_CONTRACT.json and submission/ARCHITECTURE.md for the serving contract and starter design.
requirements: Worker and Judge run on CPUs; the model backend uses 2 dedicated GPUs.
Release hardware: H100 NVL 94 GB or H100 SXM 80 GB.
Qwen3.6-27B served by vLLM 0.24.0 and 192 SWE-bench Lite tool environments.
Disk: about 230 GB for SWE-bench images, 55.6 GB for model files, and 30 GB for the backend image.
Host tools: Docker with Compose v2, the repository virtual environment, jq, and flock.
A CONNECT proxy at 127.0.0.1:18080 that reaches the agent model API.
Hidden and public Direct baselines measured on the current backend boot, plus a registered candidate-history store.
serving.evaluation: Measures valid executable tool steps per minute across all workflows. Protocol transparency, one-to-one forwarding, request success, valid-step proportion, waiting, backend work per step, and accounting checks must pass.
serving.result_intro: Optimize an OpenAI-compatible scheduling gateway between concurrent coding agents and a fixed Qwen3.6-27B backend.
serving.metric_summary: The score is the total number of valid executable steps completed across all workflows during an exact 1,800-second window, divided by 30 minutes. A completed tool return counts regardless of its exit code.
serving.setting: The workload runs 192 distinct SWE-bench Lite coding agents concurrently, each capped at 100 steps. Agents alternate between model requests and tool execution against one fixed vLLM 0.24.0 backend serving Qwen3.6-27B with tensor parallelism across two GPUs. Work and Judge are CPU-only; the candidate changes the gateway while the model server and agent environments remain fixed. Formal evaluation uses 300 seconds of warm-up followed by a 1,800-second scored window.

interface.name: Outputs
interface.description: Listen on `0.0.0.0:${PORT}` and forward each accepted model request exactly once, preserving its backend response and streaming order. An optional `/programs/release` endpoint handles program cleanup locally.
